scope: Theorem 3.6 (Global quadratic fit) of the manuscript “Two limit cycles for quintic Liénard systems” (preprints/two-limit-cycles-for-quintic-lienard-systems-September-24-2026/two-limit-cycles-for-quintic-lienard-systems-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 33941e46486c5fef), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every r > 0 and every pair (M, v) satisfying |M| < r and |v| < 1, there is a unique finite pair (λ, κ) ∈ R2 such that H(λ, κ, r) = M, Hr(λ, κ, r) = v. The fitted parameters depend jointly smoothly on (M, v, r) in this open domain. Equivalently, the smooth map (λ, κ, r) 7−→ (H(λ, κ, r), Hr(λ, κ, r), r) (3.26) is a diffeomorphism from R2 × (0, ∞) onto {(M, v, r) : r > 0, |M| < r, |v| < 1}. At every model arc, P, Q, R, S, G > 0. In particular, fitted parameters converge to a finite pair whenever their data converge to an interior point of this domain, even when the width varies.
